origin: Opus 5 sign-off round 2 ruling on the 13 pre-existing literal-### occurrences
ruling: Engine fix, not a content fix. The Japanese originals show a genuine typographic distinction -- guide-book pp.50-54 use bold heading-weight 'titled steps' (red PART 4 badges) while p.29 and most of the book use regular-weight 'sentence steps'. The translator's `N. ### title` faithfully encodes that, so editing translations/*.md would destroy source information and shift the chars/lines goldens for no benefit. The content tier is not involved and no golden regeneration is required.

tasks.title: Block-parse heading-shaped list-item content so guide-book pp.50-54 step titles render as headings
tasks.prompt:
You are implementing the single fix task of M1 sign-off round 2 for the SXC-1 Trainer.
Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. HEAD is e334ee3 and fully green (content-check 242/242,
check-site 37/37). This is a narrow grammar extension, ruled on by the Opus design agent.

YOU OWN EXACTLY THESE FOUR FILES:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/src/SXC1/Content/Markdown.hs
    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/app/View/Blocks.hs
    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/test/CheckContent.hs
    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/static/index.html          (ADDITIVE rules only -- see the constraint below)

Touch nothing else. Do NOT change Stats.hs, Outline.hs, Corpus.hs, translations/*.md,
scripts/check-site.sh or scripts/browser-check.mjs.

THE DEFECT
13 lines in translations/guide-book.md have the shape `N. ### <title>` -- an ordered-list
marker followed by a heading marker on the SAME line:

    p.50  lines 1553, 1564, 1573        p.53  line 1664
    p.51  line 1585                      p.54  lines 1705, 1709, 1715, 1721, 1725
    p.52  lines 1636, 1643, 1649

Per the current grammar the `(.*)` after the list marker becomes the item's INLINE content
(`liContent`), which is never block-parsed, so the `#` characters reach the reader as
literal text. Browser-confirmed today: p.50 -> 3, p.51 -> 1, p.52 -> 3, p.53 -> 1,
p.54 -> 5 literal `###` occurrences. All 13 are ordered-list items; there are zero
bullet-marker cases anywhere in the corpus.

THE RULING (why we fix the engine, not the translation)
I compared the Japanese originals. This is a REAL typographic distinction in the source
document, not a translator slip:

  * guide-book p.29 (source `3. Press the REC button to enter Sampling mode.`) -- the
    original shows a blue numbered badge followed by regular-weight body text. A
    "sentence step".
  * guide-book p.50 (source `1. ### In Sampling mode ... select RESAMPLING`) -- the original
    shows a red numbered badge followed by a BOLD, larger-weight step title, with the
    supporting figures and annotations beneath it. A "titled step".

The `###` therefore encodes information that is genuinely present in the printed manual.
Editing translations/guide-book.md to strip it would destroy that information (and shift the
chars/lines goldens for no benefit), so the content tier is NOT involved. The fix belongs in
the parser. This also moves the grammar TOWARD CommonMark, where `1. ### foo` is a heading
inside a list item.

WHAT TO DO
1. Markdown.hs -- extend the list-item rule: when a list item's own first-line content is
   itself heading-shaped (`headingLineOf` matches it), emit it as a `Heading` block at the
   head of that item's `liChildren` and leave `liContent` empty, instead of putting the raw
   text in `liContent`. Apply it to ordered and bullet items alike (only ordered ones occur).
   Reuse the anchor-less nested-heading path e334ee3 already added: these headings MUST get
   an empty anchor, MUST NOT consume the page's anchor-slug supply, and MUST NOT enter the
   outline.
2. View/Blocks.hs -- make sure an item whose `liContent` is empty renders cleanly (no stray
   empty inline wrapper) and that the heading child renders as a real heading element with no
   `id`, exactly as blockquote-nested headings already do.
3. index.html -- a bare `h3` as the first child of an `li` may inherit heading margins that
   push it away from its number. You may ADD a small rule set for headings inside list items
   (e.g. `.page-body li > h1, .page-body li > h2, .page-body li > h3, .page-body li > h4
   { margin-top: 0; ... }`) to keep the title on the same visual line as its step number.
   You may NOT modify or delete any existing rule, and you may not touch anything outside the
   <style> block. The existing reader-styles verification greps must all still pass.
4. CheckContent.hs -- update and widen:
   a. The nested-heading count assertion moves from `guide-book == 3` to `guide-book == 16`
      (3 blockquote headings + 13 list-item step titles); startup-guide/midi/oss stay 0.
   b. Widen the literal-hash guard to ALSO cover `liContent` (and table cells), i.e. every
      inline position in the corpus. Remove the comment exempting `liContent`. After this
      fix the guard must hold everywhere with no exclusions.
   c. Add an assertion that the 13 step titles exist as Heading blocks inside list items on
      guide-book pp. 50, 51, 52, 53, 54 with the per-page counts 3, 1, 3, 1, 5.

INVARIANTS THAT MUST NOT MOVE (all green at e334ee3)
  * Golden stats unchanged for all four documents:
        chars   111559 / 29145 / 7372 / 42533      lines 2356 / 567 / 160 / 388
        pages       71 /    15 /    6 /    16      headings 188 / 51 / 8 / 6
        figures    190 /    43 /    4 /     0      tables    20 /  5 / 7 / 0
        sections    29 /    21 /    6 /     5      subsections 78 / 27 / 1 / 0
        parts        5 /     0 /    0 /     0
    (`headings` is a raw `^#`-anchored line count, so `N. ###` lines never contributed to it
    and must still not.)
  * The golden 7-group guide-book outline and its five part titles are unchanged.
  * The pinned anchors on pp. 41/42/43/47 are unchanged.
  * ORDERED-LIST NUMBERING IS PRESERVED. This is the easiest thing to break: moving content
    into liChildren must not disturb the item's start number. guide-book p.50 must still
    render steps 1,2,3; p.54 steps 1..5; and p.29 -- which has no `###` -- must still render
    `<ol start="3">` with steps 3 and 4.
  * check-site.sh stays 37/37 and browser-check.mjs stays green, including the 108-route
    sweep and the 390x844 no-overflow assertions.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
  * `./scripts/build-site.sh` succeeds, -Wall clean.
  * Zero literal `###` in the rendered DOM of guide-book pp. 50, 51, 52, 53 and 54, and each
    step title renders heading-weight next to its number. Check with:
        ./scripts/serve-site.sh --port 8341 &
        for p in 50 51 52 53 54; do google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox \
          --user-data-dir=$(mktemp -d) --virtual-time-budget=9000 --dump-dom \
          "http://127.0.0.1:8341/#/m/guide-book/p/$p" | grep -o '###' | wc -l; done
    Paste before/after counts. Also take a screenshot of p.50 and describe how the step
    numbers and titles sit relative to each other -- if the CSS addition was needed, say so.
  * `./scripts/check-site.sh` exits 0; content-check reports its new total (>= 242).
  * NEGATIVE CONTROL, performed and reported: revert only the Markdown.hs change, rebuild,
    and confirm the widened literal-hash guard FAILS naming the 13 lines; then restore.
  * Report the rendered `<ol start=...>` values for p.29, p.50 and p.54 to prove numbering
    survived.
